program: Integrated primary care, behavioral health and insurance access
priceScope: Full annual recipient cost against conditional clinical-care and signed household-resource benefits; not entire portfolio or next-gift expected value.

what: Doctors Care provides primary and behavioral health care plus insurance and resource navigation in Littleton.
It accepts insured and uninsured patients with sliding fees, rather than providing uniformly free care.
A conditional clinical-plus-net-resource reference is about $9.78M per better life.
strengths: The original FY2025 filing provides matched clinic-client and visit counts.
Current fees, insured/public alternatives and expanded age eligibility were checked.
The model includes negative patient costs and tests outside payer and volunteer resources.
reservations: Clinic clients, coverage clients and outreach touchpoints overlap and are not additional unique cohorts.
Incremental health utility and work-resource changes remain judgments, not local causal measurements.
Whole annual cost includes coverage/navigation beyond the limited modeled clinic channel.

sections.what: Doctors Care, EIN 84-1150815, combines primary care, behavioral health, care coordination and coverage assistance. Current new-patient eligibility is newborn through age64; older filings describe up to50. Medicaid, CHP+, private insurance and uninsured patients are accepted. The correct donor route is own get-involved page with a ColoradoGives iframe; its linked endpoint returned HTTP200, no transaction made. The unavailable /donate path is not used.
sections.monitoring: Original FY2025 clinic served2,569 clients through7,920 visits. Coverage assistance served898 clients through1,228 appointments, which may overlap clinic patients. More than6,000 ambassador touchpoints are not unique health outcomes. Request deduplicated households, program overlap, Denver county, completed care, clinical change, treatment alternatives, fees/time and actual net work resources. Placeholder homepage patient stories are not causal evidence.
sections.qualitative: Primary care and behavioral health can improve function and access, but no recipient-specific utility or mortality coefficient was found. The model uses .8 client-to-household/primary-affected-person conversion, .3 incremental care versus alternatives, .4 health response and .03 utility for one year, all judgments. One household's primary clinical benefit is represented, not summing every family member automatically. Other primary-care/FQHC providers, public/insured care and counseling are alternatives. Coverage-only, vaccine and other portfolio benefits remain unmeasured, not zero.
sections.cost: FY2025 full functional expenses $3,393,823 with blank netted fundraising/gaming/COGS. FY2024 $3,231,491 and FY2023 $2,989,134 give mean $3,204,816. Recognized program expense $2,790,718 combines clinical and client services, not an allocated clinic-only cost. Whole annual cost against a clinical subset is a partial-channel reference, not a complete portfolio estimate or next-donation price. A $4M full-social-resource sensitivity allows for donated provider time and uncounted outside resources; not an observed wage bill.
sections.funding: June2026 fees range $20–$160 for all visits, with additional lab/implant costs; inability to pay does not remove time burdens. The observed average3.08 visits/client is not uniform dose. Judged $75 annual net copay/time cost and .0005 stress apply to every exposed household, even failed benefits. Judged $500 net work resources for a fraction of incremental households exclude taxes, benefit withdrawal and commuting/work costs; not salaries of survivors. Positive gains receive .5 overlap adjustment, all losses remain full, and work/access costs are joint logged. Central medical cash savings are zero as an explicit unmeasured conservative hypothesis, with positive and adverse cases—not proof of no benefit. Separate public/insurer/provider losses include only additional outside resources, avoiding duplication of recipient expenses already in C. Next-gift capacity and volunteer hours are unknown.

model.costScope: Whole FY2025 annual recipient functional cost against limited clinical partial benefits; combined-program recognized costs and social-resource sensitivities are not marginal gift prices.
model.geographicAttribution: Littleton clinic serves beyond its location; g .95 judged beneficiary share within fixed ten-county Denver CBSA19740, not observed residence or all-Colorado share.
model.formula: Health = N × unique × b × eligible × completion × response × q × finite discounted T × g minus full exposed harm. Joint signed net household work/medical resources less full access costs logged once; distinct outside payer resources localized once. Price=10C/(health + income equivalents) when positive.
model.counterfactual: Other primary-care/FQHC providers, public or insurance-covered care, covered counseling and other enrollment assistance without Doctors Care.
model.attribution: b .3 incremental access separate from clinical response; .8 conversion explicitly judged because unique clients are not household counts. All exposed negative harms/costs retained at b0.
model.uncertainty: No empirical local causal utility or disposable-income calibration. Coverage clients may overlap; outside costs, geographic residence and gift capacity missing.
model.nativeOutcomes: Matched FY2025 2,569 clinic clients/7,920 visits;898 coverage clients/1,228 appointments;6,000 ambassador touchpoints not added. Counts are delivery, not successful incremental clinical outcomes.
